args: sam toMultiAlign --help
exit: 0
--- stdout
Convert pairwise alignments in SAM format to a single alignment in fasta format

Insertions relative to the reference are omitted, so all sequences in the output are the same ( = reference)
length.

Example usage:
	gofasta sam toMultiAlign -s aligned.sam -o aligned.fasta

If you want, you can trim (and optionally pad) the output alignment to coordinates of your choosing:
	gofasta sam toMultiAlign -s aligned.sam --start 266 --end 29674 --pad -o aligned.fasta

If --samfile and --outfile are not given, the SAM file is read from stdin and the alignment is written to
stdout, e.g.:
	minimap2 -a -x asm20 --score-N=0 reference.fasta unaligned.fasta | gofasta sam toMultiAlign > aligned.fasta

Usage:
  gofasta sam toMultiAlign [flags]

Aliases:
  toMultiAlign, tomultialign, toma

Flags:
  -s, --samfile string   SAM file to read (default "stdin")
  -o, --outfile string   Where to write the alignment (default "stdout")
      --start int        1-based first position (in reference coordinates) to keep in the output. Bases before it are omitted, or replaced with N if --pad
      --end int          1-based last position (in reference coordinates) to keep in the output. Bases after it are omitted, or replaced with N if --pad
      --pad              If --start and/or --end, replace the trimmed-out regions with Ns, else replace external deletions with Ns
  -w, --wrap int         Wrap the output alignment to this number of nucleotides wide. Omit this option not to wrap the output.
      --strict           Stop with an error at the first record that can't be processed, instead of warning and skipping it
  -t, --threads int      Number of threads (and CPUs) to use (with no flag, all CPUs are used)
  -h, --help             help for toMultiAlign
--- stderr
